newsitem.title: USA: Electronic commerce still short of trust - panel.
newsitem.headline: Electronic commerce still short of trust - panel.

text.p: While some computer savvy 30-something professionals regularly buy goods over the Internet, most consumers are still far from willing to trust the Net with their credit cards numbers.

Visa International Inc., which is pursuing more than a dozen electronic commerce ventures around the world, did a survey in the past month and found only 4 percent of adult credit card holders have ever purchased anything via the Internet.
"Consumers are not ready," said Visa International Chief Executive Officer Edmund Jensen, speaking to executives at a conference here about the digital economy held by Business Week magazine.
He said another survey found that 48 percent of personal computer users believe the Internet will never be safe for commercial payments.

Just as indicative of the low level of trust in Internet-based electronic commerce, 65 percent of the 200 or so executives assembled at the Business Week conference told a survey that they are reluctant to use the Internet for payment or transactions.
And yet Visa, Charles Schwab & Co., Wells Fargo Co. and others find that Internet-based payment and stock trading programmes they have started are very succesful among a certain group of people.

Visa has 13 successful "stored value" card programmes in which credit cards are equipped with microchips to calculate value taken from or added to the card. Next year it will launch an Internet-based secure commerce programme.

Charles Schwab's "Web trading" programme launched in March has grown to 100,000 users without advertising, said Dawn Lepore, chief information officer. They trade stocks, Treasury bonds, mutual funds, options and the like.
But like Jensen, Lepore said critical to success is building trust through branding and security assurances.
"Right now, nothing is more important than building trust," Jensen said.

At Wells Fargo bank, some 110,000 of its customers use the Internet for banking. Wells Fargo, like Visa, continues to work on security and encryption methods in standards organisations and on its own.
